LESSON: READING ALOUD: DIALOGUE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.5 Reading for Information (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building • Inferri
Topic 2.7: Reading Aloud: Dialogue
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Aloud: Dialogue, part of Reading 2.5 Reading for Information (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building • Inferri in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why is reading important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify characters in a dialogue for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud: Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate speed and accuracy in reading a dialogue,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud: Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop interest in reading a variety of texts for language acquisition.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud: Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner contributes to group decision-making when discussing

the characters in the dialogue.

• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner engages in collective learning when conducting a reader’s theatre to read

a dialogue at an appropriate speed and with accuracy.
